newsitem.title: JAPAN: E.Asia Grain-Japan to resume buying after holidays.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Grain-Japan to resume buying after holidays.

text.p: Japan will resume buying grain this week after the Golden Week holiday season although it has already covered up to 80 percent of its U.S. corn requirements for the July-September shipment, traders said on Monday.
"Local end-users are returning to the market after the long holidays. The gradual rises in U.S. cash prices and freight rates are also motivating them to buy," a trader in Tokyo said.
Japanese corn premiums were quoted at around 89 to 90 U.S. cents a bushel over the CBOT May futures contract, they said.
China is also continuing to sell corn to Japan, but its prices are still relatively less competitive against U.S. origin in 1997 than last year, traders said.
Chinese corn export prices were seen averaging around US$135 a tonne FOB Dalian over the last three months, they added.
In South Korea, corn buyers will probably stay out of the market this week as they are believed to have purchased their requirements out to September, traders said.
"We are looking for new crop as we have covered our needs for old crop. Therefore we have no need to hurry buying at this stage," a trader with a major Korean feed milling firm said.
Rising feed inventories in the domestic market caused by slow consumption was also seen as another factor depressing domestic corn demand, together with a bearish price outlook.
The slowdown in feed consumption stems from lagging domestic pork and beef demand due to Korea's sluggish economy and the prospect of the pork market's opening to imports from July.
U.S. Gulf/Japan freight rates for Panamax-sized vessels were quoted at around $21.25 per tonne, traders said.

An official with the Pan Ocean Shipping Co Ltd in Korea said freight rates from the Pacific Northwest were flat at $12 a tonne over the past week for nearby shipments of Panamax-sized cargoes. The rates from the U.S. Gulf for nearby shipments of Panamax-sized vessels were also unchanged at $22 a tonne.
